scope: Primary-source literature audit. Statements below distinguish published results, recent reported formalization/preprints, and our proposed finite experiment. No independent replay of the cited analytic or Lean proofs was performed.

establishedResults.title: Zeros of the derivatives of the Riemann zeta-function
establishedResults.statement: RH is equivalent to the absence of zeros of zeta' in 0 < Re(s) < 1/2.
establishedResults.experimentMapping: The denominator of ds/da=1/zeta'(s) exposes precisely the local inverse obstruction at derivative zeros.
establishedResults.limitation: Our three branches with real a in [0,1] cannot exclude every derivative zero. General critical values zeta(s) need not be real or in this interval.

establishedResults.title: The Riemann hypothesis is true up to 3*10^12
establishedResults.statement: Rigorous interval arithmetic verifies that every zeta zero beta+i*gamma with 0 < gamma <= 3*10^12 has beta=1/2.
establishedResults.experimentMapping: This is a model for a complete finite-range certificate, rather than a display of selected accurate roots.
establishedResults.limitation: Our height-10-to-30 computations are already inside this established range. Reproducing them supplies tool validation, not new RH progress. This audit does not claim this is the latest verification record.

establishedResults.title: a-Points of the Riemann zeta-function on the critical line
establishedResults.unconditionalStatement: For each fixed nonzero complex a, asymptotically at most one-half of the nontrivial solutions of zeta(s)=a lie on Re(s)=1/2.
establishedResults.separateConditionalStatement: The zero-percent conclusion requires an additional spacing condition on the ordinates of zeta zeros.
establishedResults.experimentMapping: Off-line motion for nonzero target a belongs to established a-point theory; it neither contradicts RH nor makes our observed zeta=1 point novel.

recentAiWork.status: OpenAI-reported result and Lean formalization; not independently proof-audited or executed in this audit
recentAiWork.reportedScope: The document reports a fixed zero-free half-plane Re(s)>7/8 for zeta and every Dirichlet L-function, and finite-order Hecke L-functions over Q(sqrt(-3)); relevant poles at s=1 are excluded. The paper's later applications are outside that formalization's scope.
recentAiWork.experimentMapping: A verified imported zero-free theorem could serve as a mathematical exclusion overlay for zeros (target a=0). It does not exclude nonzero a-points and must not be applied to the a>0 moving branches.
recentAiWork.caution: Comparator challenge files are specifications, so a placeholder in one comparator does not by itself assess the separate proof implementation. No claim about all zeros being on Re(s)=1/2 follows from a 7/8 bound.

recentAiWork.provider: Anthropic/Claude, as credited in the primary paper
recentAiWork.title: A new proof that more than 2/3 of the zeros of the Riemann zeta function are simple and on the critical line
recentAiWork.status: Recent primary preprint with a separate human proof; journal acceptance and full proof validation were not established in this audit
recentAiWork.statement: The paper proves an unconditional asymptotic lower proportion C0=3/2-cot(1/sqrt(2))/sqrt(2)=0.6725007... for zeros that are both simple and on the critical line.
recentAiWork.attribution: Lamzouri credits an earlier Claude-generated argument, verified by Levent Alpoge and Ralph Furman, and supplies a different proof.
recentAiWork.experimentMapping: Simplicity supplies nonzero zeta' at starting zeros, supporting local inverse branches. A proportion theorem does not certify all zeros or guarantee continuation of our selected branches to a=1.
recentAiWork.caution: This is not an OpenAI result. This audit does not claim the entire analytic theorem has been formally verified.

proposedBoundedCertificate.status: Our proposed next engineering/mathematical validation step, not a claim from the cited papers
proposedBoundedCertificate.objective: Certify the three specific continuation paths in the existing finite viewport, including two boundary exits and the surviving a=1 endpoint.
obligations: Implement interval enclosures for zeta and zeta' with a rigorously bounded Euler-Maclaurin remainder.
Construct overlapping parameter slabs and complex boxes; validate existence and uniqueness of the local root for each slab using interval Newton or a suitable parameterized contraction certificate.
Exclude zero from the derivative enclosure throughout each certified tube.
Prove overlaps identify the same branch from a certified initial root, without reseeding.
Certify boundary crossing brackets separately from solver failure and retain explicit failure records if an obligation cannot be established.
proposedBoundedCertificate.optionalSpeiserFacingExperiment: Certify the zero count of zeta' in a specified closed box inside 0<Re(s)<1/2 using boundary enclosures and the argument principle; boundary nonvanishing must be proved.
proposedBoundedCertificate.limitation: A successful finite certificate validates only its stated tubes or box. It does not prove RH, supply a new all-height theorem, or turn phase-color patterns into a proof.
